legal_issues: Whether a Section 9 CIRP petition can be entertained when the Corporate Debtor raised documented disputes regarding the quality and timely delivery of supplied goods prior to the issuance of the statutory demand notice under Section 8(1).
ratio_decidendi: 1. ABSTRACT LEGAL RULE: An application for initiation of insolvency under Section 9 is strictly non-maintainable if the Corporate Debtor has raised a genuine, contemporaneous dispute regarding the quality or delivery of goods prior to the service of the Section 8 demand notice. 2. STATUTORY INTERPRETATION: The statutory threshold of a 'pre-existing dispute' under Sections 8 and 9 encompasses contestations over goods specifications and delivery schedules raised before statutory demand, including those preceding the enactment of the IBC itself. 3. EVIDENTIARY TEST APPLIED: The summary jurisdiction of the Adjudicating Authority excludes the trial of disputed factual particulars, such as verifying substandard quality or calculating delay in supply. 4. DEFINITIVE CONCLUSION: Because documented quality disputes had been communicated as early as September 2016, well prior to the Section 8(1) notice of September 2017, the application was barred by a pre-existing dispute.
operative_order: The appeal is dismissed without any order as to costs.
summary: Operational Creditor R. S. Fuel Pvt. Ltd. appealed the NCLT Kolkata Bench order dated 21 November 2019 dismissing its Section 9 application against Ankit Metal & Power Ltd. on the grounds of a pre-existing dispute. The NCLAT observed that the Corporate Debtor had replied to a legal notice as early as 22 September 2016 raising disputes regarding substandard coal quality and delayed deliveries, long before the Section 8(1) demand notice dated 30 September 2017 and prior to the IBC's commencement. Holding that the summary insolvency jurisdiction cannot investigate complex factual disputes regarding goods quality, the NCLAT affirmed the dismissal.

case_title: Landmark Realty vs. Siroya Developers Pvt. Ltd.
material_facts: 1. PARTY IDENTITIES: Landmark Realty is the Appellant/Operational Creditor, and Siroya Developers Pvt. Ltd. is the Respondent/Corporate Debtor. 2. COMMERCIAL TRANSACTION: Claim for operational debt recovery regarding transactions between the parties culminating in civil litigation for money recovery. 3. DEFAULT METRICS: Default amount and specific date of default not specified; appellant claimed debt recovery and respondent alleged pre-existing dispute via a pending civil suit. 4. STATUTORY TIMELINES: Demand Notice under Section 8(1) of the IBC was issued on 19th January, 2019. 5. FACTUAL EVIDENCE: Prior to the issuance of the Demand Notice, the Appellant had filed Civil Suit No. 1149 of 2018 for recovery of money against the Corporate Debtor before the Bombay City Civil Court at Dindoshi, Mumbai; Appellant also relied on a letter alleging the Corporate Debtor admitted the claim. 6. PROCEDURAL HISTORY: Section 9 application filed by Appellant was rejected by the Adjudicating Authority (NCLT Mumbai Bench) on 4th November, 2019 on grounds of pre-existing dispute; NCLAT condoned a 9-day filing delay and heard the appeal.
legal_issues: Whether a Section 9 application under the IBC is maintainable when the Operational Creditor had instituted a civil money recovery suit against the Corporate Debtor prior to the issuance of the statutory Demand Notice under Section 8(1), despite an alleged letter of claim admission.
ratio_decidendi: 1. ABSTRACT LEGAL RULE: The pendency of a prior civil suit for recovery of money filed by an operational creditor against a corporate debtor constitutes an undeniable pre-existing dispute, barring the initiation of Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process under Section 9. 2. STATUTORY INTERPRETATION: CIRP is not a recovery proceeding, money suit, or substitute for civil litigation as previously established; an operational creditor cannot bypass a pre-existing dispute under Section 8/9 via IBC when formal civil proceedings for debt recovery are already pending. 3. EVIDENTIARY TEST APPLIED: The existence of a prior pending civil suit on record before a court of competent jurisdiction conclusively demonstrates a pre-existing dispute that cannot be resolved or adjudicated on merits regarding alleged debt admission letters by the Adjudicating Authority under Section 9 summary proceedings. 4. DEFINITIVE CONCLUSION: Because a money recovery suit was admittedly filed prior to the Section 8(1) notice and remains pending, the Adjudicating Authority rightly rejected the Section 9 application.
operative_order: Delay of 9 days in preferring the appeal is condoned; Company Appeal (AT) (Insolvency) No. 25 of 2020 is dismissed; clarified that orders passed by the Adjudicating Authority or Appellate Tribunal shall not be relied upon for the determination of the civil suit pending before the court of competent jurisdiction.
summary: Landmark Realty appealed an order dated 4 November 2019 by NCLT Mumbai rejecting its Section 9 IBC application against Siroya Developers Pvt. Ltd. on the ground of a pre-existing dispute. Prior to issuing its Section 8(1) demand notice on 19 January 2019, Landmark Realty had filed Civil Suit No. 1149 of 2018 for money recovery before the Bombay City Civil Court. Landmark argued that the debt had been admitted in a letter, but the NCLAT reiterated that CIRP is not a recovery proceeding. Finding the pending pre-notice money suit to constitute a clear pre-existing dispute, the NCLAT upheld the rejection and dismissed the appeal.
